# Promoted to repo memory: roadmap-h2

Cite these in .sofar/repo.md by qualified handle — `roadmap-h2 M<n>` —
which is how `sofar doctor` sees that a promoted fact reached repo memory.

- **M1** (2026-09-22T17:43:49.230Z) — Branch bindings are unreliable when several sessions share one checkout, and the damage shows up a day later as a torn session. sofar_end_session rehomes the branch binding to the ending session's initiative, so with N sessions on `main` it is last-writer-wins: on 2026-09-22 three sessions moved `main` in two hours (r1-fixes, then rust-core, then memory-lead). Two consequences. (1) A session's OPENING events — session_started and the first command_runs — land in whatever the binding said at start, then re-homing moves the rest, leaving orphans behind: session 063dc84a has 3 events in drive-visibility and 211 in memory-lead, and `sofar doctor` reports FAIL — session spans 2 initiatives (torn, live). Fix it by appending a session_ended for that id to the record holding the orphans; it is an append recording a true fact, never a rewrite, and it is the hygiene of the record that HOLDS the strays, not of the initiative that owns the session. (2) Avoid causing it: pass `--initiative` (or the tool's `initiative`) explicitly on every write, and do the write-back with `sofar event append` from a per-initiative git worktree rather than from the shared checkout, which is the only mitigation that kept the binding still.
- **M2** (2026-09-29T07:52:29.775Z) — round3-runner's tests run with `bun run test` (= bun test ./test/*.test.ts) from scenario5-launch-bench/runner/. Bare `bun test` also collects test/fixtures/*/hidden-tests, which fail without BENCH_APP_DIR, so never read those failures as a runner regression.
